questionText: The marketing team submitted a detailed _______ of last quarter's campaign results.
explanation: After "a detailed", a noun is needed, and "analysis" is the noun.

questionText: Mr. Park's _______ to the sales department was announced at the staff meeting.
explanation: A possessive ("Mr. Park's") must be followed by a noun.

questionText: Customers have praised the company for its _______ in resolving billing disputes.
explanation: After the possessive "its", a singular noun is required.

questionText: The committee will review all _______ for the regional manager position next week.
explanation: "All" is followed by a plural noun, and "applications" fits the meaning.

questionText: The auditors raised concerns about the _______ of the quarterly figures.
explanation: After "the", a noun is needed; "accuracy" is the uncountable noun that fits.

questionText: Please _______ your timesheet to the payroll office by Friday afternoon.
explanation: After "please", the base form of the verb is used for the request.

questionText: The new software is designed to _______ the process of ordering office supplies.
explanation: After "to" in an infinitive, the base verb is required.

questionText: Ms. Alvarez asked the team to _______ the contract before sending it to the client.
explanation: "Asked ... to" is followed by the base form of the verb.

questionText: The conference center offers _______ parking for all registered attendees.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "parking".

questionText: Only _______ employees may enter the restricted laboratory.
explanation: The participle "authorized" works as an adjective meaning "approved".

questionText: The restaurant is known for its _______ service and reasonable prices.
explanation: An adjective is needed to describe the noun "service".

questionText: Dr. Chen gave a _______ presentation on emerging markets in Southeast Asia.
explanation: An adjective must come between "a" and the noun "presentation".

questionText: The shipment will arrive _______ at the warehouse on Tuesday morning.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb "will arrive".

questionText: Sales have risen _______ since the new pricing plan was introduced.
explanation: An adverb modifies the verb phrase "have risen".

questionText: The instructions must be followed _______ to avoid damaging the equipment.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the passive verb "be followed".

questionText: The board of directors was _______ divided over the proposed merger.
explanation: An adverb can modify the participle "divided".

questionText: The company _______ more than 200 new employees since January.
explanation: "Since January" requires the present perfect tense.

questionText: Our technicians _______ the printer problem twice this week.
explanation: "This week" with a repeated action in an unfinished period takes the present perfect.

questionText: The manager _______ the new schedule at yesterday's meeting.
explanation: "Yesterday" signals a finished past action.

questionText: Last year, the firm _______ its headquarters from Boston to Denver.
explanation: "Last year" is a finished time, so the past simple is required.

questionText: The training session _______ at 9:00 a.m. tomorrow in Room 204.
explanation: "Tomorrow" signals the future, so "will begin" is correct.

questionText: By the end of the year, the factory _______ over one million units.
explanation: "By the end of the year" calls for the future perfect.

questionText: When the inspector _______ the building, he will check the fire exits.
explanation: In a time clause that refers to the future, the present simple is used.

questionText: Please call me as soon as the shipment _______.
explanation: After "as soon as", use the present simple for a future event.

questionText: By the time the auditors arrived, the accountant _______ all the records.
explanation: The past perfect shows an action completed before another past action.

questionText: The IT department _______ the servers right now, so please wait.
explanation: "Right now" signals the present continuous.

questionText: If the supplier delivers late, we _______ the order.
explanation: A first conditional with the present simple in the "if" clause takes "will".

questionText: If Ms. Ito had submitted the report on time, she _______ the bonus.
explanation: A third conditional uses "would have" plus the past participle.

questionText: All expense reports _______ by the finance team every Monday.
explanation: The reports receive the action, so the passive is required; the plural subject takes "are".

questionText: The new product line _______ at the trade fair next month.
explanation: The product line cannot launch itself, so the passive is needed.

questionText: The merger _______ by regulators before the end of the quarter.
explanation: The merger is approved by someone else, which requires the passive.

questionText: The list of candidates _______ on the bulletin board.
explanation: The subject is the singular "list", not "candidates".

questionText: Each of the managers _______ responsible for a separate department.
explanation: "Each of" takes a singular verb.

questionText: The number of customer complaints _______ decreased this year.
explanation: "The number of" is singular and takes "has".

questionText: Neither the director nor the assistants _______ aware of the schedule change.
explanation: With "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, "assistants".

questionText: The office will be closed _______ December 25 and January 1.
explanation: "Between ... and" links two points in time.

questionText: Please arrive _______ 8:30 a.m. to complete the registration.
explanation: "By" sets a deadline for the arrival.

questionText: The renovation work will continue _______ the end of next month.
explanation: "Until" shows an action that lasts up to a point in time.

questionText: The refund will be processed _______ five business days.
explanation: "Within" shows the time limit for completing the action.

questionText: The marketing department is _______ the third floor of the main building.
explanation: "On" is used with floors of a building.

questionText: The new copier is located _______ the break room and the supply closet.
explanation: "Between" is used for two items.

questionText: All visitors must comply _______ the company's security policy.
explanation: The verb "comply" takes the preposition "with".

questionText: Ms. Gomez is responsible _______ training all new hires.
explanation: "Responsible for" is the standard collocation.

questionText: The proposal is similar _______ the one we rejected last year.
explanation: "Similar to" is the correct pairing.

questionText: Employees may be eligible _______ a pension after ten years of service.
explanation: "Eligible for" is the standard collocation.

questionText: The shipment was delayed owing _______ severe weather conditions.
explanation: "Owing to" means "because of".

questionText: The meeting was postponed _______ the director was ill.
explanation: "Because" introduces a clause with a subject and verb.

questionText: _______ the budget was limited, the team still completed the project successfully.
explanation: "Although" introduces a contrast and is followed by a clause.

questionText: You may leave early _______ you finish all of your assigned tasks.
explanation: "Provided that" introduces a condition and fits the meaning.

questionText: The package will not be shipped _______ payment has been received.
explanation: "Not ... until" means the action waits for the condition.

questionText: _______ the new policy takes effect, all staff must complete the safety course.
explanation: "Before" introduces a clause about the time order.

questionText: Mr. Reyes will lead the workshop, _______ Ms. Kim will handle registration.
explanation: "While" links two simultaneous or contrasting actions.

questionText: _______ the heavy traffic, the guests arrived on time for the banquet.
explanation: "Despite" is followed by a noun phrase; the others need a clause.

questionText: The flight was canceled _______ the storm.
explanation: "Because of" is followed by a noun phrase such as "the storm".

questionText: _______ their different backgrounds, the two founders share a common vision.
explanation: "In spite of" takes a noun phrase.

questionText: Ms. Lee asked the assistants to finish _______ work before noon.
explanation: A possessive determiner is needed before the noun "work".

questionText: The director introduced _______ to the new staff members.
explanation: The subject and object are the same person, so the reflexive pronoun is needed.

questionText: Please send the invoice to Mr. Davis or _______ assistant.
explanation: A possessive determiner is needed before "assistant".

questionText: The two companies agreed to share the cost between _______.
explanation: "Themselves" refers back to the subject of the sentence.

questionText: The employee _______ won the sales award will receive a bonus.
explanation: "Who" refers to a person and acts as the subject of "won".

questionText: The report, _______ was completed last week, is available online.
explanation: "Which" refers to the thing "report" in a non-defining clause.

questionText: We need a supplier _______ prices are lower than those of our current vendor.
explanation: "Whose" shows possession: the supplier's prices.

questionText: The client with _______ we signed the agreement has offices in Seoul.
explanation: After a preposition ("with"), the object form "whom" is used for a person.

questionText: The _______ customers were given a full refund.
explanation: People who feel disappointment are "disappointed".

questionText: The presentation was so _______ that many attendees took notes.
explanation: The presentation provides information, so "informative" is the correct adjective.

questionText: All _______ documents must be signed by a witness.
explanation: The documents are attached by someone, so the past participle is used.

questionText: The manager was _______ by the team's rapid progress.
explanation: The manager received the impression, so the passive participle fits.

questionText: The company plans _______ a new branch in Osaka next year.
explanation: "Plan" is followed by the infinitive.

questionText: Ms. Torres suggested _______ the deadline by one week.
explanation: "Suggest" is followed by a gerund.

questionText: The staff is looking forward to _______ the new CEO next week.
explanation: "Look forward to" is followed by a gerund.

questionText: Mr. Kato avoided _______ the issue during the negotiation.
explanation: "Avoid" is followed by a gerund.

questionText: Employees are required _______ their badges at all times.
explanation: "Be required" is followed by the infinitive.

questionText: This year's profits are _______ than last year's.
explanation: The word "than" signals a comparative form.

questionText: The new model is _______ efficient than the previous one.
explanation: "More ... than" forms the comparative for a long adjective.

questionText: This is _______ successful campaign in the company's history.
explanation: A superlative with "the" is needed for "in the company's history".

questionText: Of all the applicants, Ms. Wu has _______ experience.
explanation: The comparison among many applicants requires the superlative.

questionText: We received _______ applications for the open position.
explanation: "Applications" is countable and plural, so "many" is correct.

questionText: There is not _______ time left to finish the audit.
explanation: "Time" is uncountable, so "much" is used.

questionText: _______ of the board members voted against the proposal.
explanation: "Most of" is followed by a plural noun phrase.

questionText: The company has _______ branches abroad, so international travel is rare.
explanation: "Few" is used with countable nouns and has a negative meaning.

questionText: Visitors _______ sign in at the front desk before entering.
explanation: "Must" expresses a required action.

questionText: You _______ submit the form today if you want the discount.
explanation: "Should" gives advice or a recommended action.

questionText: The supervisor suggested that the report _______ revised before Monday.
explanation: After "suggested that", the base form is used (subjunctive).

questionText: Employees _______ in the program receive extra training.
explanation: A reduced relative clause uses the past participle: "who are enrolled".

questionText: The job requires planning, organizing, and _______ team projects.
explanation: A list needs the same form; the others in the list are gerunds.

questionText: Ms. Huang is both an experienced engineer and a _______ manager.
explanation: Both items after "both ... and" must be the same type: noun phrases with adjectives.

questionText: You can pay either by credit card _______ by bank transfer.
explanation: "Either ... or" is the correct pair.

questionText: The proposal was not only creative _______ also affordable.
explanation: "Not only ... but also" is the correct pair.

questionText: The project was complex; _______, the team finished it ahead of schedule.
explanation: "Nevertheless" shows a contrast between difficulty and success.

questionText: Sales fell sharply; _______, the company cut its marketing budget.
explanation: "Consequently" shows the result of the sales drop.

questionText: The store is offering a _______ of 20 percent on all electronics this weekend.
explanation: A discount is a price reduction.

questionText: Please keep your _______ as proof of purchase.
explanation: A receipt is a paper that proves a payment.

questionText: The company will _______ the new regulations starting next month.
explanation: "Implement" means to put a plan or rule into action.

questionText: All payments are due within thirty days of the invoice _______.
explanation: "Invoice date" is a standard noun phrase.

questionText: The firm hired a consultant to _______ its operating costs.
explanation: After "to", the base verb is needed and the meaning fits.

questionText: Before signing the lease, Mr. Ito asked the landlord to _______ the terms.
explanation: "Clarify" means to make something clear.

questionText: The airline offered passengers a _______ for the inconvenience caused by the delay.
explanation: Compensation is payment given for a problem or loss.

questionText: The warehouse manager must _______ the inventory every quarter.
explanation: To reconcile inventory means to match records with actual stock.

questionText: The CEO's speech _______ the importance of customer loyalty.
explanation: "Emphasized" means gave special importance to.

questionText: Our firm specializes _______ corporate tax law.
explanation: "Specialize in" is the correct collocation.

questionText: Please _______ the attached document and return it by Thursday.
explanation: To complete a document means to fill it in fully.

questionText: The hotel requires a credit card to _______ a reservation.
explanation: To guarantee a reservation is to secure it.

questionText: The contract will _______ automatically unless either party gives notice.
explanation: A contract renews when it is extended for another term.

questionText: Employees are _______ to use the stairs during the fire drill.
explanation: "Advised" means strongly recommended.

questionText: The seminar is _______ to all employees, not only managers.
explanation: After "is", an adjective is used; "open to" means available to.

questionText: The cost of materials has _______ by ten percent since March.
explanation: "Increase" can be intransitive, meaning it grew; "raised" needs an object.

questionText: The vendor was unable to _______ the order because the item was out of stock.
explanation: To fulfill an order means to complete and deliver it.

questionText: All new employees must _______ a background check before their first day.
explanation: "Undergo" means to experience a required process.

questionText: The manager was asked to _______ the budget proposal at the board meeting.
explanation: "Present" is the base verb meaning to show or introduce formally.

questionText: A _______ number of attendees requested vegetarian meals.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "number".

questionText: Our office hours are from 9 a.m. _______ 5 p.m., Monday to Friday.
explanation: "From ... to" gives a range of time.

questionText: The lecturer will _______ the findings of the study at the conference.
explanation: "Summarize" means to give the main points briefly.

questionText: Applicants should _______ a résumé and two letters of recommendation.
explanation: "Enclose" means to include with a letter or package.

questionText: The new tax law will _______ small businesses the most.
explanation: "Affect" is the verb meaning to influence.

questionText: The company is committed _______ reducing its carbon emissions.
explanation: "Committed to" is followed by a gerund or noun.

questionText: The warranty is _______ for two years from the date of purchase.
explanation: After "is", an adjective is needed; "valid" means legally effective.

questionText: Mr. Silva was _______ to the position of regional director last month.
explanation: "Appointed to a position" is the standard collocation.

questionText: The hotel manager apologized for the _______ caused by the power outage.
explanation: After "the", a noun is needed; "inconvenience" is the noun that fits the meaning.

questionText: Participation in the wellness program is _______ for all full-time employees.
explanation: After "is", an adjective is needed to describe "participation".

questionText: The _______ of the new warehouse will create about fifty jobs.
explanation: After "the", a noun is needed, and "construction" fits the meaning.

questionText: Ms. Ramirez gave a clear _______ of how the software works.
explanation: After the adjective "clear", a noun is required.

questionText: Strict _______ to safety rules is required in the chemical plant.
explanation: After the adjective "strict", a noun is needed; "adherence to" is the collocation.

questionText: The company's _______ on foreign suppliers has grown over the past decade.
explanation: After the possessive, a noun is needed, and "reliance on" is the collocation.

questionText: The board will _______ the final decision on Thursday.
explanation: After the modal "will", the base verb is used.

questionText: New employees are encouraged to _______ their ideas during team meetings.
explanation: After "to" in the infinitive, the base verb is needed.

questionText: The manager decided to _______ the training session until next week.
explanation: After "to", the base form of the verb is needed.

questionText: Cost-saving measures will _______ the company to remain profitable.
explanation: After the modal "will", the verb "enable" is used with an object and "to".

questionText: The _______ report will be sent to all shareholders next week.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "report".

questionText: The _______ results of the survey will be published next month.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "results".

questionText: It is _______ that all documents be signed before the deadline.
explanation: After "It is", an adjective is needed.

questionText: Mr. Wong is a _______ salesperson who exceeds his targets every month.
explanation: An adjective is needed to describe the noun "salesperson".

questionText: The software update is _______ with both Windows and Mac systems.
explanation: After "is", an adjective is needed; "compatible with" is the collocation.

questionText: Please speak _______ so everyone in the hall can hear you.
explanation: An adverb modifies the verb "speak".

questionText: The new policy was _______ welcomed by the employees.
explanation: An adverb modifies the passive verb "was welcomed".

questionText: The report is _______ complete, but a few charts are missing.
explanation: An adverb modifies the adjective "complete".

questionText: The shipping costs were _______ higher than we had budgeted.
explanation: An adverb modifies the comparative "higher".

questionText: The bank _______ at 9 a.m. and closes at 4 p.m. on weekdays.
explanation: A routine schedule uses the present simple.

questionText: The department _______ its monthly target for three months in a row.
explanation: "For three months in a row" up to now needs the present perfect.

questionText: Ms. Obi _______ the company in 2015 and became CEO in 2022.
explanation: Finished past years such as 2015 require the past simple.

questionText: The new store _______ next Saturday with a special sale.
explanation: "Next Saturday" is in the future.

questionText: While the technician _______ the network, the power suddenly went out.
explanation: The past continuous describes an action in progress when another action interrupted.

questionText: We _______ for a reliable distributor for several months.
explanation: "For several months" with an ongoing action takes the present perfect continuous.

questionText: If I were you, I _______ the contract carefully before signing.
explanation: A second conditional uses "would" plus the base verb.

questionText: _______ the shipment arrive late, please notify the customer immediately.
explanation: Inverted "Should" replaces "If" in a formal first conditional.

questionText: Had the company invested earlier, it _______ a larger market share today.
explanation: "Had the company invested" is an inverted third conditional.

questionText: The conference room _______ for the board meeting all day tomorrow.
explanation: The room is reserved by someone, so the passive is needed.

questionText: Several errors _______ in the first draft of the contract.
explanation: The errors are found by someone else, so the passive is used.

questionText: The new hires _______ an orientation packet upon arrival.
explanation: "Give" with a person as the subject of the passive needs "will be given".

questionText: The manager and her assistant _______ at the conference this week.
explanation: Two subjects joined by "and" take a plural verb.

questionText: The results of the survey _______ that customers prefer faster delivery.
explanation: The plural subject "results" takes the plural verb "show".

questionText: Every employee in the sales departments _______ a company laptop.
explanation: "Every employee" is singular.

questionText: The committee, along with several advisors, _______ the plan next week.
explanation: The subject is the singular "committee", not the "advisors".

questionText: The seminar will be held _______ Room B on Friday.
explanation: "In" is used with a named room.

questionText: Ms. Chang travels to London _______ business every month.
explanation: "On business" is a fixed phrase.

questionText: The price is _______ to change without notice.
explanation: "Subject to" means likely to change depending on conditions.

questionText: Please send your application _______ the human resources department.
explanation: "Send to" marks the recipient.

questionText: The conference was well attended _______ the bad weather.
explanation: "Despite" is followed by the noun phrase "the bad weather".

questionText: The funds will be distributed _______ the five regional offices.
explanation: "Among" is used for more than two items.

questionText: The merger took place _______ the CEO's strong objection.
explanation: "Despite" introduces a contrast with the noun phrase.

questionText: The manager is in charge _______ the entire logistics operation.
explanation: "In charge of" is the standard phrase.

questionText: Employees must refrain _______ using personal phones on the production floor.
explanation: "Refrain from" is followed by a gerund.

questionText: The proposal depends _______ the approval of the finance committee.
explanation: The verb "depend" takes "on".

questionText: The new CEO is known _______ turning around struggling companies.
explanation: "Known for" means famous because of something.

questionText: The audit revealed discrepancies _______ the two sets of records.
explanation: "Between" is used for two things being compared.

questionText: The seminar was canceled _______ too few people registered.
explanation: "Because" introduces the reason.

questionText: _______ the contract is signed, the work cannot begin.
explanation: "Until" shows the condition that must be met first.

questionText: The product is popular _______ it is inexpensive and easy to use.
explanation: "Because" introduces the reason for the popularity.

questionText: _______ you have any questions, please contact the help desk.
explanation: "Should you have" is a formal inverted condition.

questionText: The proposal will be accepted _______ the budget is approved.
explanation: "Provided" before "the budget is approved" introduces a condition.

questionText: You must wear a helmet _______ you are on the construction site.
explanation: "Whenever" means every time that.

questionText: The two managers decided to handle the complaint _______ .
explanation: The reflexive pronoun refers to the two managers.

questionText: The red folder is mine, and the blue one is _______ .
explanation: The possessive pronoun replaces "her folder".

questionText: The proposal was written by Ms. Tanaka and _______ .
explanation: After "and" in the object position of "by", the object pronoun is used.

questionText: The consultant _______ we hired last year has opened her own firm.
explanation: "Whom" refers to a person in the object position.

questionText: This is the office _______ the board meets every month.
explanation: "Where" refers to a place and takes the place of "in which".

questionText: The merger, _______ was announced on Monday, surprised investors.
explanation: A non-defining clause with commas takes "which", not "that".

questionText: The _______ manager decided to meet with each employee.
explanation: "Newly appointed" is the adverb plus participle that modifies "manager".

questionText: Anyone _______ in the training must register by Friday.
explanation: The person feels interest, so the past participle is used.

questionText: The documents _______ in the folder are confidential.
explanation: A reduced relative clause: "that are contained" or "which contain"; here "contained" suits the passive meaning with "in the folder".

questionText: The firm is considering _______ a second office in Madrid.
explanation: "Consider" is followed by a gerund.

questionText: Ms. Park managed _______ the contract despite the tight deadline.
explanation: "Manage" is followed by the infinitive.

questionText: Thank you for _______ us your catalog so quickly.
explanation: After the preposition "for", a gerund is used.

questionText: The board postponed _______ on the budget until next quarter.
explanation: "Postpone" is followed by a gerund.

questionText: The supervisor reminded the staff _______ the machines before leaving.
explanation: "Remind someone" is followed by the infinitive.

questionText: The second proposal is _______ expensive than the first one.
explanation: "Less ... than" is the comparative pattern.

questionText: Our new printer is twice _______ as the old one.
explanation: "Twice as ... as" needs the base adjective.

questionText: The _______ we invest, the greater our return will be.
explanation: The pattern "the more ..., the greater ..." is a double comparative.

questionText: She is one of _______ negotiators in the industry.
explanation: "One of the" is followed by a superlative.

questionText: _______ employee must wear an ID badge in the building.
explanation: "Every" is followed by a singular noun.

questionText: We have _______ time before the client arrives, so let's review the slides.
explanation: "Little" is used with uncountable nouns; here it gives a limited amount.

questionText: _______ of the two proposals met the budget limit.
explanation: "Neither of the two" is used for two items.

questionText: Only a _______ of employees attended the optional workshop.
explanation: "A few" is used with a plural countable noun, meaning some.

questionText: Passengers _______ not use electronic devices during takeoff.
explanation: "May not" expresses a prohibition in a formal notice.

questionText: The system _______ be restarted after the update is installed.
explanation: "Must be restarted" is the modal passive for a requirement.

questionText: The shipment _______ have arrived by now; let's check the tracking number.
explanation: "Should have arrived" means it was expected to arrive.

questionText: The company will _______ a new product next spring.
explanation: To launch a product means to introduce it to the market.

questionText: Please _______ the form with your name and address.
explanation: "Fill out" a form is a common phrasal verb.

questionText: The factory had to _______ production because of a shortage of raw materials.
explanation: To suspend production means to stop it temporarily.

questionText: Customers can _______ their orders online at any time.
explanation: To track an order means to follow its progress.

questionText: The manager asked the team to _______ their expenses carefully.
explanation: To monitor expenses means to watch them closely.

questionText: The new employee's _______ includes handling customer inquiries.
explanation: After the possessive, a noun is needed; the singular fits "includes".

questionText: The seminar will _______ practical tips for improving customer service.
explanation: "Cover" means to include or discuss topics.

questionText: The invoice shows the total _______ due, including tax.
explanation: "Amount due" is the sum that must be paid.

questionText: Several candidates were _______ for the final interview.
explanation: To be shortlisted means to be selected for the final group.

questionText: The manufacturer issued a _______ of the faulty brake parts.
explanation: A recall asks customers to return defective products.

questionText: Mr. Fujita was asked to _______ the meeting while the chair was away.
explanation: To preside over a meeting means to lead it formally.

questionText: The two firms signed a _______ agreement to share research costs.
explanation: "Joint agreement" is an adjective plus noun.

questionText: Only authorized staff may _______ access to the server room.
explanation: "Gain access" is the standard collocation.

questionText: The company's profits _______ sharply after the new competitor entered the market.
explanation: "Plummeted" means fell very quickly.

questionText: We apologize for the _______ in delivering your order.
explanation: After "the", a noun is needed; "delay in delivering" is the standard phrase.

questionText: The tickets are _______ until the end of the month.
explanation: After "are", an adjective is needed.

questionText: Ms. Evans is _______ for the quarterly sales report; please contact her.
explanation: "In charge" is a fixed phrase.

questionText: We need to find a more _______ way to store customer data.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "way".

questionText: The CEO announced that the company would _______ its operations into Asia.
explanation: To expand means to grow bigger or reach new areas.

questionText: All claims must be _______ within thirty days of the incident.
explanation: To file a claim means to submit it officially.

questionText: The training will be _______ by an experienced consultant from Zurich.
explanation: The passive "will be conducted" fits a session led by someone.

questionText: Please make sure all _______ are turned off before you leave.
explanation: A plural noun is needed, and "appliances" fits turning off equipment.

questionText: Our new software will _______ the need for manual data entry.
explanation: To eliminate means to remove completely.

questionText: The restaurant owner decided to _______ a loan to renovate the kitchen.
explanation: "Take out a loan" means to borrow money.

questionText: The hotel's rooms are _______ with free Wi-Fi and a mini fridge.
explanation: "Equipped with" means supplied with equipment.

questionText: Applications must be _______ no later than May 31.
explanation: After "must be", a past participle is needed.

questionText: The two departments will _______ on the new advertising campaign.
explanation: To collaborate means to work together.

questionText: A _______ of volunteers helped to organize the charity fundraiser.
explanation: "A number of" is a quantity phrase followed by a plural noun.

questionText: The CEO's resignation took effect _______ .
explanation: An adverb at the end of the clause modifies "took effect".

questionText: Employees who work overtime will be _______ at one and a half times their regular rate.
explanation: "Compensated" means paid for work or a loss.

questionText: We are happy to _______ you to our annual dinner.
explanation: "Invite someone to an event" is the standard use.

questionText: Before the merger, the two companies were fierce _______ .
explanation: After the adjective "fierce", a plural noun is needed.

questionText: The updated brochure will be _______ at the entrance to all visitors.
explanation: The passive participle "distributed" fits after "will be".

questionText: Due to unforeseen _______, the product launch has been rescheduled.
explanation: "Unforeseen circumstances" is a fixed business phrase.

questionText: Revenues for the year _______ initial projections by twelve percent.
explanation: "Exceeded" means went beyond.

questionText: The sales team is _______ to meet the target by the end of the month.
explanation: "Is expected to" is a passive structure.
